answer: The Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm provides a haven for decentralized networks by implementing voting mechanisms that prevent Sybil attacks. In this system, agents must reach a summit of agreement on a proposal, and any deviations from this consensus are considered a fault. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to simultaneously alter the votes of multiple agents, but this would be akin to trying to erode a karst landscape without sufficient groundwater flow, ultimately leading to a collapse of their efforts.
